confirmed: migrate() is deleted from bootstrap.ts and nothing calls it: startup runs the migration runner only, so there is no second competing startup migration mechanism
the checksum is a SHA-256 of canonical migration source text read from the build artifact, never Function.prototype.toString()
the runner owns the ledger and creates the table only when absent
history is validated read-only before any write, then re-read and re-validated inside the immediate write lock
a pre-ledger journal is not treated as already migrated: the baseline convergence runs first and version 1 is recorded afterwards
each migration's up() and its ledger row are written in the same immediate transaction, so a failure never advances the ledger
a future version, a tampered name, a tampered checksum, a missing applied version, a non-contiguous history and a non-contiguous registry each raise a distinct MigrationError
coordinatorReview.findingRaisedAndWithdrawn: The coordinator flagged the explicit .ts import specifiers and the added allowImportingTsExtensions option in apps/web/tsconfig.json as a convention deviation, because the repository holds zero .ts-extension imports elsewhere and tsconfig.json is not in the phase guide's modify list. Verification confirmed the worker's stated reason: db-concurrent-init.test.ts spawns child Node processes with --experimental-strip-types that await import() the real TypeScript modules, and Node's ESM resolver does not search for extensions, so the explicit specifier is functionally required. The option is legal because tsconfig.base.json already sets noEmit true. The worker had recorded it as deviation 1 and amended the plan before the implementation commit. No defect; the observation was withdrawn.
